question: Find the volume of a cylinder whose base radius is 12.5 cm and whose height is (4)/(5) of the base radius.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Height** (h) = 4/5 × 12.5 = 10 cm

**Volume** = π × r² × h

**Volume** = π × 156.25 × 10 = 1562.5 π cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1562.5 π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base **radius** (r) = 12.5 cm

**Height** (h) = 4/5 × radius

**Formula Used:**

**Volume** of a **cylinder** = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38b12a1b6939087ceb8d70f2e7ff7a9768ad65fbe0d3b35c76805ea42351e50f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ h = (4/5) × 12.5 cm

⇒ h = 4 × 2.5 = 10 cm

⇒ Volume = π × (12.5)² × 10

⇒ Volume = π × 156.25 × 10

⇒ Volume = 1562.5 π cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1562.5 π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of Cylinder

The area of the side surface of the cylinder is given by 2πrh.

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cylinder

The sum of the CSA and the area of the two circular bases: 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r).

Volume of a Cone

For the same radius and height, the volume of a cone is exactly one-third of the volume of a cylinder: (1/3)πr²h.</p
